Divarasib monotherapy demonstrated superior efficacy over first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors, lowering the risk of disease progression or death by 42% and the overall risk of death by 44%, in the phase III Krascendo 1 study1,2
At the time of primary analysis, divarasib achieved a median overall survival of approximately 18 months, compared to 12 months for sotorasib or adagrasib1,2
No new safety signals were observed with divarasib; the most common treatment-related adverse events were mainly low grade and manageable1,2
Data presented as a late-breaking abstract during a Presidential Symposium at the 2026 ESMO Congress and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine1,2

title: Roche (RHO) KRAS Drug Cut Death Risk 44% vs Current SOC in Phase III
